name: Metronidazole
route_note: Oral tablets or suspension, IV infusion, rectal suppositories, vaginal gel and topical gel/cream for rosacea.
targets: DNA (via reductively activated nitro radicals formed by pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase pathways)

discovery.note: Synthesised as part of work on azomycin (2-nitroimidazole) derivatives for trichomoniasis.

tagline: Nitroimidazole for anaerobic bacteria, trichomoniasis, giardiasis and amoebiasis
summary: Metronidazole is a nitroimidazole introduced by Rhône-Poulenc in 1960 for trichomoniasis and later found to be highly active against anaerobic bacteria. It is a standard drug for anaerobic infections, bacterial vaginosis, protozoal infections and Helicobacter pylori regimens.
mechanism: Metronidazole is a prodrug that diffuses into cells and is activated only in organisms with low-redox-potential electron-transport proteins, such as ferredoxin reduced by pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase in anaerobic bacteria and protozoa.

Reduction of its nitro group produces short-lived nitro radical anions and other intermediates that cause DNA strand breaks and destabilise the helix, killing the cell. Aerobic human cells and aerobic bacteria do not activate it efficiently, giving selective toxicity. Resistance is uncommon in anaerobes but may involve nim genes or reduced activation.
uses: Anaerobic infections (intra-abdominal, pelvic, brain abscess, aspiration pneumonia), often with other agents
Clostridioides difficile infection (when first-line agents are unavailable)
Rosacea (topical) and surgical prophylaxis in colorectal surgery

history.title: Azomycin
history.detail: The 2-nitroimidazole azomycin is isolated from Streptomyces, inspiring Rhône-Poulenc's nitroimidazole programme.

history.title: Anaerobic activity noticed
history.detail: A patient's acute ulcerative gingivitis resolving during trichomoniasis treatment reveals metronidazole's activity against anaerobes.

history.title: C. difficile guidance change
history.detail: IDSA/SHEA guidelines no longer recommend metronidazole as first-line for adult C. difficile infection.

serious: Peripheral and optic neuropathy with prolonged use
safety.boxed_warning: Metronidazole has been shown to be carcinogenic in mice and rats; avoid unnecessary use and reserve for approved indications (US label).

facts: Labels have long advised avoiding alcohol because of a possible disulfiram-like reaction, although controlled studies have questioned this effect.
